input.strategy_title: Surface model deployment status in the RHOAI Dashboard
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists deploying models through the Dashboard cannot tell whether a
deployment is healthy without leaving the console. InferenceService state is
only visible via `oc get inferenceservice` or by reading Kubernetes events,
which most Dashboard users cannot access. Support cases regularly begin with
"my model has been Pending for an hour" — information the platform already has
but does not surface.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users see a deployment status (Ready, Progressing, Failed) for each deployed model in the Dashboard model serving views. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Users can open a status detail view showing the underlying condition messages and recent events for a failed or progressing deployment. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Displayed status reflects the actual InferenceService state within 30 seconds of a change, without a manual page reload. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Users can filter and sort the deployed models list by status. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation explains each status value and the first troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe

## Out of Scope

- Alerting or notifications on status transitions
- Status history / timeline views
- ModelMesh deployments (KServe InferenceService only)

## Open Questions

None blocking — KServe already exposes the needed conditions on the
InferenceService status; this strategy is about surfacing them.

# Surface InferenceService deployment status in Dashboard model serving views

## Description

This epic delivers deployment status visibility for KServe
InferenceServices inside the RHOAI Dashboard. Data scientists will see a
computed status — Ready, Progressing, or Failed — for each deployed model in
the model serving views, and can open a detail view showing the underlying
InferenceService condition messages and recent Kubernetes events for
deployments that are failing or still progressing. The status shown reflects
the actual InferenceService state within 30 seconds of a change, without a
manual page reload, and the deployed models list can be filtered and sorted
by status.

The Dashboard reads InferenceService resources through the Kubernetes API
(the Dashboard owns no data plane); status is derived from the conditions and
events KServe already exposes on the InferenceService resource. No KServe
code changes are required.

## Scope

- Compute and display a deployment status (Ready / Progressing / Failed) per
  deployed model in the Dashboard model serving views.
- Status detail view for a deployment, showing the underlying InferenceService
  condition messages and recent events — used primarily for failed or
  progressing deployments.
- Keep displayed status within 30 seconds of the actual InferenceService state
  without requiring a manual page reload (the refresh mechanism — polling
  interval vs. Kubernetes watch — is an implementation decision for the
  Dashboard team).
- Filter and sort the deployed models list by status.
- Scope is limited to KServe InferenceService deployments; ModelMesh
  deployments, status alerting/notifications, and status history / timeline
  views are out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a deployed model whose InferenceService is ready, the Dashboard model
  serving views show status Ready for it.
- Given a deployment that is progressing or failed, the views show
  Progressing or Failed respectively, and the displayed status matches the
  actual InferenceService state — measured by comparison against the
  InferenceService status conditions (e.g. Ready, PredictorReady) that KServe
  exposes (passive-component validation for KServe).
- Given a failed or progressing deployment, the user can open a status detail
  view showing the underlying condition messages and recent events for that
  deployment.
- Given a change in InferenceService state, the displayed status reflects the
  new state within 30 seconds, without a manual page reload.
- Given the deployed models list, the user can filter it by status and sort it
  by status.
- Automated tests cover status computation from InferenceService conditions
  and events for the Ready, Progressing, and Failed cases.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): status per deployed model in model serving views — primary
  scope.
- HLR-2 (P0): status detail view with condition messages and recent events —
  primary scope.
- HLR-3 (P1): 30-second freshness without manual reload — primary scope.
- HLR-4 (P2): filter and sort by status — bundled here because it shares the
  deployed-models-list UI surface with HLR-1 and is not independently
  deferrable.

# Document deployment status values and Failed-deployment troubleshooting

## Description

This epic delivers the product documentation for the Dashboard deployment
status feature: a doc topic that explains each deployment status value shown
in the Dashboard model serving views (Ready, Progressing, Failed) and the
first troubleshooting steps a user should take when a deployment shows
Failed. The documentation is written through the Red Hat docs content
process, against the status display, condition messages, and events that the
Dashboard implementation actually surfaces.

## Scope

- Author a product documentation topic explaining each deployment status
  value displayed in the Dashboard model serving views.
- Document the first troubleshooting steps for a Failed deployment (e.g.
  where to find the status detail view, how to read the underlying condition
  messages and recent events).
- Validate all documented content for technical accuracy against the
  implemented Dashboard status feature and the InferenceService conditions
  and events it surfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation explains each status value (Ready, Progressing, Failed) shown
  for deployed models in the Dashboard.
- Documentation includes first troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments,
  referencing the status detail view and the condition messages and events it
  shows.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented Dashboard
  status feature and matches the statuses, messages, and events actually
  displayed.
- Documentation follows the Red Hat docs content process and is published in
  the product documentation set.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P2): product documentation explains each status value and first
  troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments — full coverage of this epic.
